title: American Retrieval vs YoCierge vs Codes Health (2026)
summary: Compare American Retrieval, YoCierge, and Codes Health for medical record retrieval in 2026, covering AI analysis, case management integrations, completeness checks, and flat-fee pricing.
body_markdown:
Law firms handling personal injury, medical malpractice, and mass tort cases know that medical records can make or break a settlement. The traditional retrieval process drags on for months, buries paralegals in follow-up calls, and often delivers incomplete documentation that turns into trial surprises. Three services approach this differently: American Retrieval brings decades of provider relationships, YoCierge offers technology-driven workflows with a broad integration catalog, and Codes Health combines AI-powered retrieval with case analysis in a single platform. Knowing where they differ helps plaintiff firms pick the right partner for their caseload.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Codes Health combines medical record retrieval with AI-powered case analysis and human verification in one workflow, reducing the need for separate retrieval and review vendors


-


American Retrieval brings more than 30 years of established provider relationships and says its integrations with copy services help it process requests across a large share of U.S. medical providers


-


YoCierge offers a broad native case management integration catalog, including Filevine, Clio, SmartAdvocate, and Litify


-


All three services use flat-fee pricing models without per-page charges, though specific rates require custom quotes


-


Codes Health's Missing Record Review flags documentation gaps before delivery, and comparable proactive gap detection was not identified in the competitor materials reviewed


-


The Filevine integration is live, letting Codes Health users submit requests, track status, and receive records inside their case files


-


Incomplete authorizations are a leading cause of denied requests across all providers, which makes pre-submission validation worth evaluating closely


## **Understanding the Core: What Each Medical Records Retrieval Company Offers**


Medical records retrieval companies sit between law firms and healthcare providers, managing the authorization, request, follow-up, and delivery work that eats paralegal time. Each brings distinct strengths.


### **Codes Health: AI-Powered Retrieval and Analysis**


Founded in 2024 by MIT and Yale graduates,[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) approaches retrieval as an AI-native platform built for modern plaintiff practices, with backing from Y Combinator.


The platform pairs retrieval operations with automated case analysis. Rather than just delivering documents, Codes Health extracts diagnoses, treatments, providers, expenses, and care events from unstructured medical records. That processing includes breach-of-care flagging for malpractice cases and future expense extraction for damages calculations.


Retrieval runs through multiple channels including claims clearinghouses, patient portals, custodian integrations, and traditional fax and phone outreach. The service works toward complete records in a couple of weeks rather than the months typical of traditional workflows.


Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team keeps building out additional workflows and products, so the platform continues to evolve, improve, and grow more comprehensive as the demands of modern legal practices change.


### **American Retrieval: Traditional Strengths**


American Retrieval brings more than 30 years of experience to medical record retrieval, having been founded in 1993. U.S. Legal Support acquired the company in January 2025, adding national footprint and enterprise resources.


American Retrieval says its direct integrations with copy services such as CIOX help it process requests across a large share of U.S. medical providers. That provider network, built over three decades, supports consistent retrieval across major health systems, and the company emphasizes personalized service through dedicated account representatives rather than call centers.


Its RecordsHub portal provides OCR-processed searchable PDFs with text search, highlight, and annotation capabilities. The service focuses on reliable document delivery rather than an AI analysis layer.


### **YoCierge: Technology-Driven Retrieval**


YoCierge, founded in 2017, processes approximately 400,000 records annually and has built a broad case management integration catalog, with native connections to platforms including Filevine, Clio, SmartAdvocate, Litify, MyCase, CasePeer, Neos, and Smokeball.


YoCierge expanded its Instant Medical Record Locator service to Nevada and Connecticut in March 2026, giving access to participating statewide networks. For facilities inside those networks, retrieval can happen within hours.


The company holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications along with CARIN accreditation. Its YoSign system handles HIPAA authorization through proprietary e-signature workflows.


## **Beyond the Basics: AI-Powered Medical Record Request and Analysis**


Whether a service stops at retrieval or extends into analysis determines whether a firm needs one vendor or two for case preparation.


### **The AI-Human Hybrid Approach**


Codes Health runs an AI-human hybrid model where automated systems process records and human experts verify findings before delivery. That addresses a real gap: general AI platforms like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review, and running clinical documentation through them produces confident answers that fall apart under scrutiny. Codes Health's platform is purpose-built for this work and analyzes medical records with high precision.


The AI pipeline extracts structured information from thousands of pages of unstructured clinical documentation. Medical, legal, and operational specialists then validate those findings before records reach the requesting firm.


American Retrieval delivers OCR-processed documents for manual review. YoCierge provides AI summaries and chronological reordering through features like ReChron and its Medical Expense Table. Codes Health differentiates through litigation-focused analysis, including breach-of-care flagging, and through the human verification layer applied to AI output.


### **Automating Chronologies and Summaries**


For high-volume personal injury firms,[case chronology creation](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/software-solutions-high-volume-personal-injury) is a significant paralegal burden. Codes Health automatically organizes, compiles, and summarizes case records chronologically, grouping patient encounters and bills by visit.


That automation also exposes gaps in treatment or documentation, letting teams request specific missing records rather than repeating broad retrieval requests. Document summaries condense individual records into key findings while preserving links back to source material.


### **Identifying Breaches in Care with AI**


For medical malpractice screening, Codes Health's breach-of-care flagging identifies potential departures from medical standards, which supports early case strength assessment and expert witness preparation.


The system also surfaces pre-existing conditions that affect case valuation, missed appointments that may weigh on damages arguments, and documented future medical needs for settlement negotiations. Those insights turn medical records from raw evidence into usable case intelligence.


## **HIPAA Compliance in Medical Records Retrieval**


All three services operate as HIPAA-compliant platforms, though certification depth and published security documentation vary.


### **Security Certifications Compared**


YoCierge publishes the most extensive certification list among the three, with SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and CARIN-related compliance. American Retrieval maintains HIPAA compliance. Codes Health operates as a HIPAA-compliant platform and publishes information about encryption, penetration testing, monitoring, and other security controls.


All three offer Business Associate Agreements where the vendor acts as a HIPAA business associate. Each provides encryption in transit and at rest, though specific standards and data hosting arrangements are worth confirming directly with any vendor rather than taking compliance claims at face value.


### **HIPAA-Compliant E-Signature Workflows**


Each platform provides electronic authorization workflows built for HIPAA requirements:


-


**Codes Health** offers integrated e-signature for releases of information, physician orders, and authorization forms with AI-assisted validation


-


**American Retrieval** provides portal-based electronic authorization management


-


**YoCierge** uses its proprietary YoSign system for email- or mobile number based HIPAA e-signatures


Secure document storage across all three supports continued access to retrieved materials and cuts duplicate work when the same records apply at different case stages.


## **Streamlining Legal Workflows: Integration with Case Management Systems**


Managing retrieval from inside existing case management software has a real effect on paralegal efficiency and workflow consistency.


### **The Filevine and Codes Health Integration Advantage**


Codes Health is now integrated with Filevine, letting legal teams manage medical record retrieval directly from their Filevine case files. The arrangement goes beyond a standard third-party connection, positioning Codes Health as a premium service available where legal teams already work.


Filevine users can:


-


Submit medical record requests from the relevant case file


-


Track request status and provider outreach in real time


-


Communicate with the Codes Health team without leaving the project


-


Receive completed medical records, billing, and imaging directly in the Filevine project


-


Review retrieval history and completeness status within the case workflow


That removes the context switching between case management platforms, retrieval vendor portals, email, and downloaded file folders. Requests and communications stay attached to the right matter throughout.


### **Comparing Integration Breadth**


YoCierge offers a wide integration catalog with native connections to case management systems including Clio, SmartAdvocate, Litify, MyCase, CasePeer, Neos, and Smokeball, plus document management platforms like Dropbox, Google Workspace, and Microsoft SharePoint.


American Retrieval offers Filevine integration and portal-based access through RecordsHub but does not publicly document the same breadth of native case management connections.


Codes Health provides the embedded Filevine workflow and builds custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software for high-volume customers, so firms with significant case volumes can connect their specific systems.


## **Release of Information: Forms, Processes, and Best Practices**


Incomplete authorizations are a leading cause of denied record requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can cause providers to reject a request outright and require resubmission, which creates substantial delay. When a request qualifies under HIPAA's individual right-of-access provisions, covered entities generally must act within 30 calendar days, with one possible 30-day extension in specified circumstances. Some state laws set shorter deadlines, so confirm the applicable standard when working across jurisdictions.


### **Automated Validation of Authorizations**


Codes Health's AI review catches authorization errors before submission, automatically flagging:


-


Misspellings in patient or provider names


-


Missing dates of service


-


Absent or incomplete signatures


-


Unchecked boxes for sensitive record types


-


Provider-specific requirement gaps


-


Incorrect facility information


That pre-submission validation prevents the rejections and delays that plague traditional workflows. Instead of finding an authorization problem weeks in, firms address it before the request leaves the platform.


### **Ensuring Complete and Correct Forms**


All three services provide guidance on proper authorization completion, though automation levels differ:


-


**Codes Health** uses AI-assisted validation with automatic error detection


-


**American Retrieval** provides portal-based validation for standard requirements


-


**YoCierge** validates through the YoSign e-authorization system


Provider-specific requirements add complexity. Some facilities want particular form versions, specific signature placements, or additional consent for behavioral health, HIV, or substance abuse records. Codes Health checks against provider-specific requirements, while other services may rely on more standardized processes.


## **Speed and Completeness: Differentiating Factors in Medical Record Retrieval**


Speed claims need context. No retrieval service can force a provider to respond faster than that provider chooses to move.


### **Understanding Turnaround Time Differences**


YoCierge's same-day processing refers to the timing of order submission, not record delivery. Orders submitted before 4 pm go out the same day. For facilities participating in its Instant Medical Record Locator network, retrieval can happen within hours. Standard provider-dependent requests still follow typical timelines.


American Retrieval advertises approximately 15 days for standard retrievals, reflecting its established provider relationships and persistent follow-up.


Codes Health works toward complete records in a couple of weeks rather than months, prioritizing verified completeness over partial fast delivery. That reduces the follow-up cycles that happen when initial retrievals miss critical documentation.


According to Codes Health, services promising same-day retrieval typically return only what sits immediately available electronically, leaving the firm and the client to chase the rest. That added client involvement, in the company's stated experience, is a common source of frustration and churn. Codes Health does not market same-day retrieval. It pursues the complete record set, including harder-to-reach providers, date ranges, and billing files, in a couple of weeks rather than months.


### **The Value of Persistent Follow-Up**


All three manage ongoing provider outreach, but the methods differ:


-


**Codes Health** uses multi-channel follow-up through calls, faxes, emails, and portals until records arrive, with visibility into completed outreach and next required actions


-


**American Retrieval** assigns dedicated account representatives who manage follow-up without call center routing


-


**YoCierge** processes same-day submissions with standard follow-up workflows


The gap between submission speed and actual retrieval completion matters a great deal for case preparation timelines.


### **Ensuring a Complete Record Set**


Codes Health's Missing Record Review cross-references patient medical history to identify:


-


Missing facilities that appear in clinical notes but lack requested records


-


Absent date ranges within treatment timelines


-


Missing billing records that support damages calculations


-


Documentation gaps that could create trial surprises


That completeness verification happens before records return to the firm. When gaps appear, Codes Health works with facilities to resolve them rather than delivering incomplete documentation.


Codes Health publicly documents this proactive Missing Record Review. Comparable proactive gap-detection functionality was not identified in the American Retrieval or YoCierge materials reviewed, though both provide standard retrieval verification confirming receipt of requested materials.


## **Tailored Solutions: Meeting Specific Legal Practice Needs**


Different practice areas need different retrieval and analysis capabilities.


### **Legal Practice Area Specializations**


Codes Health serves[seven legal practice areas](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/software-solutions-legal-assistants) : personal injury, mass torts, medical malpractice, workers' compensation, disability law, insurance litigation, and wrongful death.


For personal injury cases, the platform extracts treatment histories, identifies causation factors, and documents future medical needs. For malpractice matters, breach-of-care flagging supports standard-of-care analysis and expert witness preparation.


Mass tort practices benefit from running similar workflows across large plaintiff portfolios, since the AI-powered approach scales across hundreds or thousands of cases while holding analysis quality consistent.


American Retrieval serves personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice firms with traditional retrieval. Its long-established provider relationships give consistent access but call for separate analysis solutions.


YoCierge similarly serves plaintiff practices across multiple areas, emphasizing integration flexibility and submission speed.


### **Pricing Considerations**


All three use flat-fee pricing without per-page charges:


-


**Codes Health** charges a flat fee


-


**American Retrieval** offers flat rates per request


-


**YoCierge** uses volume-based flat fees regardless of page count


None publish complete public pricing, and all require custom quotes based on firm size, volume, integration requirements, and service level. Keep in mind that provider and copying charges vary substantially by jurisdiction, record format, and request type, so the retrieval fee is rarely the whole cost picture.


## **Making an Informed Choice: Selecting the Right Partner for Your Needs**


The right pick depends less on feature lists than on which part of your workflow is actually costing you. If the bottleneck is getting documents in the door and your team already has a chronology process that works, a retrieval-focused vendor covers it. If the bottleneck is what happens after the pages arrive, you need a platform that handles analysis too.


Questions worth asking any vendor before committing:


-


Does the quoted turnaround describe completed delivery, or just how fast the order gets processed?


-


Are chronologies, insights extraction, and completeness checks included, or billed separately?


-


Who verifies AI output before it reaches the case file?


-


What happens when a provider stops responding, and who does the chasing?


-


Does the platform work inside your case management system, or add another portal to log into?


### **Where Each Platform Fits**


American Retrieval suits firms that value a long track record, dedicated account representatives over call center routing, and searchable OCR delivery through RecordsHub, with analysis handled internally or through a separate vendor. YoCierge suits firms that want a wide native integration catalog, published security certifications, and AI-assisted organization and summaries layered onto retrieval. Codes Health suits plaintiff firms that want retrieval, authorization validation, completeness verification, and litigation-focused analysis handled together under one flat fee, without standing up a separate chronology workflow.


## **The Bottom Line**


Most records problems that damage a case were preventable months earlier. An authorization goes out with an unchecked box for sensitive records and comes back rejected. A fast delivery looks complete until the billing file and the specialist records turn out to be missing, and now the client is making phone calls. A chronology gets built by hand, and the treatment gap defense counsel eventually raises was sitting on page 1,400 the whole time.


American Retrieval and YoCierge both do solid retrieval work, and YoCierge layers on AI summaries and chronological reordering for firms that mainly need documents moved and organized. Codes Health is built for the failure modes above: validation that catches authorization errors before submission, persistent follow-up that pursues the complete record set in a couple of weeks rather than whatever arrives fastest, Missing Record Review that surfaces gaps before delivery, and human-verified analysis flagging pre-existing conditions, documented future expenses, and potential breaches of care. It all sits inside one flat fee.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What happens when a healthcare provider ignores a medical record request?**


For requests qualifying under HIPAA's individual right of access, covered entities generally must act within 30 calendar days, with one possible 30-day extension in specified circumstances. Requests made solely under a signed authorization do not carry the same federal timing requirement, and some state laws set shorter deadlines. When providers go quiet, retrieval services escalate through additional calls, fax reminders, email follow-ups, and direct portal requests. Persistent non-response may require involving facility compliance officers or, rarely, subpoena processes. Codes Health provides visibility into all outreach attempts and escalation status within the Filevine workflow.


### **How do these services handle radiology images and DICOM files?**


Medical imaging retrieval takes specialized handling beyond standard clinical records. YoCierge offers integrated DICOM viewer capabilities with direct SmartAdvocate integration. Codes Health retrieves imaging records through its multi-channel approach including patient portals and custodian integrations. American Retrieval handles imaging requests but does not feature integrated viewing tools. For cases requiring extensive radiology review, confirm specific imaging capabilities and delivery formats with each vendor during evaluation.


### **Can I switch retrieval vendors mid-case without losing existing records?**


Switching during active litigation takes coordination but is workable. Most services deliver records as downloadable files that stay with your firm regardless of the vendor relationship. Authorization forms signed for one vendor do not automatically transfer, so new authorizations may be needed for ongoing requests. Codes Health and YoCierge both maintain secure document storage for continued access to previously retrieved materials. When transitioning, inventory pending requests, confirm which authorizations remain valid, and coordinate handoff timing to avoid gaps.


### **How do retrieval services handle sensitive mental health or substance abuse records?**


Records protected under 42 CFR Part 2 or state mental health privacy laws require specific authorization language beyond standard HIPAA releases. All three services can retrieve these records when proper authorizations exist. Codes Health's AI validation flags when requests involve sensitive record types and checks for appropriate consent language before submission. YoCierge's YoSign system accommodates multi-consent scenarios. American Retrieval handles sensitive records through standard request processes with authorization verification. Confirm state-specific requirements for behavioral health records, since they vary by jurisdiction.


### **What quality controls exist to prevent delivery of incorrect patient records?**


Medical record mix-ups create serious legal and ethical problems. Each service implements verification to match delivered records to the requesting patient. Codes Health uses AI-assisted validation before requests are submitted and verifies retrieved materials for completeness before delivery. American Retrieval and YoCierge use standard verification comparing request details against received materials. Human review remains important regardless of vendor, since healthcare facility errors in record compilation happen independently of retrieval service quality controls.
